USA.quake_max_place: The 1964 Prince William Sound, Alaska Earthquake
USA.terrain: vast central plain, mountains in west, hills and low mountains in east; rugged mountains and broad river valleys in Alaska; rugged, volcanic topography in Hawaii
USA.climate_text: mostly temperate, but tropical in Hawaii and Florida, arctic in Alaska, semiarid in the great plains west of the Mississippi River, and arid in the Great Basin of the southwest; low winter temperatures in the northwest are ameliorated occasionally in January and February by warm chinook winds from the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains
USA.hazards_text: tsunamis; volcanoes; earthquake activity around Pacific Basin; hurricanes along the Atlantic and Gulf of America coasts; tornadoes in the Midwest and Southeast; mud slides in California; forest fires in the west; flooding; permafrost in northern Alaska is a major impediment to development. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the Hawaiian Islands, Western Alaska, the Pacific Northwest, and in the Northern Mariana Islands; Mauna Loa (4,170 m) in Hawaii and Mount Rainier (4,392 m) in Washington have been deemed Decade Volcanoes by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to their explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Pavlof (2,519 m) is the most active volcano in Alaska's Aleutian Arc and poses a significant threat to intercontinental air travel; St. Helens (2,549 m), famous for the devastating 1980 eruption, remains active today; other historically active volcanoes are mostly concentrated in the Aleutian arc and Hawaii, including (in Alaska) Aniakchak, Augustine, Chiginagak, Fourpeaked, Iliamna, Katmai, Kupreanof, Martin, Novarupta, Redoubt, Spurr, Wrangell, Trident, Ugashik-Peulik, Ukinrek Maars, Veniaminof, (in Hawaii) Haleakala, Kilauea, Loihi, (in the Northern Mariana Islands) Anatahan, (in the Pacific Northwest) Mount Baker, and Mount Hood; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

SGS.terrain: most of the islands are rugged and mountainous rising steeply from the sea; South Georgia is largely barren with steep, glacier-covered mountains; the South Sandwich Islands are of volcanic origin with some active volcanoes
SGS.climate_text: variable, with mostly westerly winds throughout the year interspersed with periods of calm; nearly all precipitation falls as snow
SGS.hazards_text: the South Sandwich Islands have prevailing weather conditions that generally make them difficult to approach by ship; they are also subject to active volcanism

TJK.terrain: mountainous region dominated by the Alay Mountains in the north and the Pamirs in the southeast; western Fergana Valley in north, Kofirnihon and Vakhsh Valleys in southwest
TJK.climate_text: mid-latitude continental, hot summers, mild winters; semiarid to polar in Pamir Mountains

CHE.terrain: mostly mountains (Alps in south, Jura in northwest) with a central plateau of rolling hills, plains, and large lakes
CHE.climate_text: temperate, but varies with altitude; cold, cloudy, rainy/snowy winters; cool to warm, cloudy, humid summers with occasional showers

SWE.lowest_point: reclaimed bay of Lake Hammarsjon, near Kristianstad
SWE.terrain: mostly flat or gently rolling lowlands; mountains in west
SWE.climate_text: temperate in south with cold, cloudy winters and cool, partly cloudy summers; subarctic in north
SWE.hazards_text: ice floes in the surrounding waters, especially in the Gulf of Bothnia, can interfere with maritime traffic

RUS.terrain: broad plain with low hills west of Urals; vast coniferous forest and tundra in Siberia; uplands and mountains along southern border regions
RUS.climate_text: ranges from steppes in the south through humid continental in much of European Russia; subarctic in Siberia to tundra climate in the polar north; winters vary from cool along Black Sea coast to frigid in Siberia; summers vary from warm in the steppes to cool along Arctic coast
RUS.hazards_text: permafrost over much of Siberia is a major impediment to development; volcanic activity in the Kuril Islands; volcanoes and earthquakes on the Kamchatka Peninsula; spring floods and summer/autumn forest fires in Siberia and parts of European Russia. Volcanoes: Kamchatka Peninsula is home to 29 historically active volcanoes, with dozens more in the Kuril Islands; Kliuchevskoi (4,835 m) is Kamchatka's most active volcano; Avachinsky and Koryaksky volcanoes, which pose a threat to the city of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, have been deemed Decade Volcanoes by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to their explosive history and close proximity to human populations; other notable historically active volcanoes include Bezymianny, Chikurachki, Ebeko, Gorely, Grozny, Karymsky, Ketoi, Kronotsky, Ksudach, Medvezhia, Mutnovsky, Sarychev Peak, Shiveluch, Tiatia, Tolbachik, and Zheltovsky; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

PER.terrain: western coastal plain (costa), high and rugged Andes in center (sierra), eastern lowland jungle of Amazon Basin (selva)
PER.climate_text: varies from tropical in east to dry desert in west; temperate to frigid in Andes
PER.hazards_text: earthquakes, tsunamis, flooding, landslides, mild volcanic activity. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the Andes Mountains; Ubinas (5,672 m) is the country's most active volcano; other historically active volcanoes include El Misti, Huaynaputina, Sabancaya, and Yucamane; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

PAK.terrain: divided into three major geographic areas: the northern highlands, the Indus River plain in the center and east, and the Balochistan Plateau in the south and west
PAK.climate_text: mostly hot, dry desert; temperate in northwest; arctic in north
PAK.hazards_text: frequent earthquakes, occasionally severe especially in north and west; flooding along the Indus after heavy rains (July and August)

NOR.quake_max_place: near Longyearbyen, Svalbard and Jan Mayen
NOR.terrain: glaciated; mostly high plateaus and rugged mountains broken by fertile valleys; small, scattered plains; coastline deeply indented by fjords; arctic tundra in north
NOR.climate_text: temperate along coast, modified by North Atlantic Current; colder interior with increased precipitation and colder summers; rainy year-round on west coast
NOR.hazards_text: rockslides, avalanches. Volcanoes: Beerenberg (2,227 m) on Jan Mayen Island in the Norwegian Sea is the country's only active volcano

ranges: Southern Alps/Kā Tiritiri o te Moana
NZL.terrain: predominately mountainous with large coastal plains
NZL.hazards_text: earthquakes are common, though usually not severe; volcanic activity. Volcanoes: significant volcanism on North Island; Ruapehu (2,797 m) has a history of large eruptions in the past century; Taranaki has the potential to produce dangerous avalanches and lahars; other historically active volcanoes include Okataina, Raoul Island, Tongariro, and White Island; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

NPL.terrain: Tarai or flat river plain of the Ganges in south; central hill region with rugged Himalayas in north
NPL.climate_text: varies from cool summers and severe winters in north to subtropical summers and mild winters in south
NPL.hazards_text: severe thunderstorms; flooding; landslides; drought and famine depending on the timing, intensity, and duration of the summer monsoons

KGZ.terrain: peaks of the Tien Shan mountain range and associated valleys and basins encompass the entire country
KGZ.climate_text: dry continental to polar in high Tien Shan Mountains; subtropical in southwest (Fergana Valley); temperate in northern foothill zone
KGZ.hazards_text: major flooding during snow melt; prone to earthquakes

KAZ.terrain: vast flat steppe extending from the Volga in the west to the Altai Mountains in the east and from the plains of western Siberia in the north to oases and deserts of Central Asia in the south
KAZ.climate_text: continental, cold winters and hot summers, arid and semiarid
KAZ.hazards_text: earthquakes in the south; mudslides around Almaty

ITA.terrain: mostly rugged and mountainous; some plains, coastal lowlands
ITA.climate_text: predominantly Mediterranean; alpine in far north; hot, dry in south
ITA.hazards_text: regional risks include landslides, mudflows, avalanches, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, flooding; land subsidence in Venice. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity; Etna (3,330 m) is Europe's most active volcano, and its flank eruptions pose a threat to nearby Sicilian villages; Etna, along with the famous Vesuvius, have both been deemed Decade Volcanoes by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to their explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Stromboli, on its namesake island, has also been continuously active with moderate volcanic activity; other historically active volcanoes include Campi Flegrei, Ischia, Larderello, Pantelleria, Vulcano, and Vulsini

IND.terrain: upland plain (Deccan Plateau) in south, flat to rolling plain along the Ganges, deserts in west, Himalayas in north
IND.climate_text: varies from tropical monsoon in south to temperate in north
IND.hazards_text: droughts; flash floods, as well as widespread and destructive flooding from monsoonal rains; severe thunderstorms; earthquakes. Volcanoes: Barren Island (354 m) in the Andaman Sea has been active in recent years

ISL.terrain: mostly plateau interspersed with mountain peaks, icefields; coast deeply indented by bays and fiords
ISL.climate_text: temperate; moderated by North Atlantic Current; mild, windy winters; damp, cool summers
ISL.hazards_text: earthquakes and volcanic activity. Volcanoes: Iceland is situated on top of a hotspot and experiences severe volcanic activity; Eyjafjallajokull (1,666 m) erupted in 2010, sending ash high into the atmosphere and seriously disrupting European air traffic; scientists continue to monitor nearby Katla (1,512 m), which has a high probability of eruption; Grimsvoetn and Hekla are Iceland's most active volcanoes; other historically active volcanoes include Askja, Bardarbunga, Brennisteinsfjoll, Esjufjoll, Hengill, Krafla, Krisuvik, Kverkfjoll, Oraefajokull, Reykjanes, Torfajokull, and Vestmannaeyjar

GEO.terrain: largely mountainous with Great Caucasus Mountains in the north and Lesser Caucasus Mountains in the south; Kolkhet'is Dablobi (Kolkhida Lowland) opens to the Black Sea in the west; Mtkvari River Basin in the east; fertile soils in river valley flood plains and foothills of Kolkhida Lowland
GEO.climate_text: warm and pleasant; Mediterranean-like on Black Sea coast

ATF.highest_point: Mont de la Dives on Ile Amsterdam
ATF.terrain: Ile Amsterdam (Ile Amsterdam et Ile Saint-Paul): a volcanic island with steep coastal cliffs; the center floor of the volcano is a large plateau Ile Saint-Paul (Ile Amsterdam et Ile Saint-Paul): triangular in shape, the island is the top of a volcano, rocky with steep cliffs on the eastern side; has active thermal springs Iles Crozet: a large archipelago formed from the Crozet Plateau is divided into two groups of islands Iles Kerguelen: the interior of the large island of Ile Kerguelen is composed of high mountains, hills, valleys, and plains with peninsulas stretching off its coasts Bassas da India (Iles Eparses): atoll, awash at high tide; shallow (15 m) lagoon Europa Island, Glorioso Islands, Juan de Nova Island: low, flat, and sandy Tromelin Island (Iles Eparses): low, flat, sandy; likely volcanic seamount
ATF.climate_text: Ile Amsterdam et Ile Saint-Paul: oceanic with persistent westerly winds and high humidity Iles Crozet: windy, cold, wet, and cloudy Iles Kerguelen: oceanic, cold, overcast, windy Iles Eparses: tropical
ATF.hazards_text: Ile Amsterdam and Ile Saint-Paul are inactive volcanoes; Iles Éparses are subject to periodic cyclones; Bassas da India is a maritime hazard because it is under water for three hours before and after high tide. Volcanoes: Reunion Island - Piton de la Fournaise (2,632 m), which has erupted many times in recent years, is one of the world's most active volcanoes; although rare, eruptions outside the volcano's caldera could threaten nearby cities

GRL.quake_max_place: near the north coast of Greenland
GRL.terrain: flat to gradually sloping icecap covers all but a narrow, mountainous, barren, rocky coast
GRL.climate_text: arctic to subarctic; cool summers, cold winters
GRL.hazards_text: continuous permafrost over northern two-thirds of the island

CHN.terrain: mostly mountains, high plateaus, deserts in west; plains, deltas, and hills in east
CHN.climate_text: extremely diverse; tropical in south to subarctic in north
CHN.hazards_text: frequent typhoons (about five per year along southern and eastern coasts); damaging floods; tsunamis; earthquakes; droughts; land subsidence. Volcanoes: China contains some historically active volcanoes including Changbaishan (also known as Baitoushan, Baegdu, or P'aektu-san), Hainan Dao, and Kunlun although most have been relatively inactive in recent centuries

CHL.terrain: low coastal mountains, fertile central valley, rugged Andes in east
CHL.climate_text: temperate; desert in north; Mediterranean in central region; cool and damp in south
CHL.hazards_text: severe earthquakes; active volcanism; tsunamis. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity due to more than three-dozen active volcanoes along the Andes Mountains; Lascar (5,592 m), which last erupted in 2007, is the most active volcano in the northern Chilean Andes; Llaima (3,125 m) in central Chile, which last erupted in 2009, is another of the country's most active; Chaiten's 2008 eruption forced major evacuations; other notable historically active volcanoes include Cerro Hudson, Calbuco, Copahue, Guallatiri, Llullaillaco, Nevados de Chillan, Puyehue, San Pedro, and Villarrica; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

CAN.terrain: mostly plains with mountains in west, lowlands in southeast
CAN.climate_text: varies from temperate in south to subarctic and arctic in north
CAN.hazards_text: continuous permafrost in north is a serious obstacle to development; cyclonic storms form east of the Rocky Mountains, a result of the mixing of air masses from the Arctic, Pacific, and North American interior, and produce most of the country's rain and snow east of the mountains. Volcanoes: the vast majority of volcanoes in Western Canada's Coast Mountains remain dormant

BTN.terrain: mostly mountainous with some fertile valleys and savanna
BTN.climate_text: varies; tropical in southern plains; cool winters and hot summers in central valleys; severe winters and cool summers in Himalayas
BTN.hazards_text: violent storms from the Himalayas are the source of the country's Bhutanese name, which translates as Land of the Thunder Dragon; frequent landslides during the rainy season

ARG.terrain: rich plains of the Pampas in northern half, flat to rolling plateau of Patagonia in south, rugged Andes along western border
ARG.climate_text: mostly temperate; arid in southeast; subantarctic in southwest
ARG.hazards_text: San Miguel de Tucumán and Mendoza areas in the Andes subject to earthquakes; pamperos are violent windstorms that can strike the pampas and northeast; heavy flooding in some areas. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the Andes Mountains along the Chilean border; Copahue (2,997 m) last erupted in 2000; other historically active volcanoes include Llullaillaco, Maipo, Planchón-Peteroa, San José, Tromen, Tupungatito, and Viedma

AFG.terrain: mostly rugged mountains; plains in north and southwest
AFG.climate_text: arid to semiarid; cold winters and hot summers
AFG.hazards_text: damaging earthquakes occur in Hindu Kush mountains; flooding; droughts

ATA.terrain: about 99% thick continental ice sheet and 1% barren rock, with average elevations between 2,000 and 4,000 m; mountain ranges up to nearly 5,000 m; ice-free coastal areas include parts of southern Victoria Land, Wilkes Land, the Antarctic Peninsula area, and parts of Ross Island on McMurdo Sound; glaciers form ice shelves along about half of the coastline, and floating ice shelves constitute 11% of the area of the continent
ATA.climate_text: the coldest, windiest, and driest continent on Earth; severe low temperatures vary with latitude, elevation, and distance from the ocean; East Antarctica is colder than West Antarctica because of its higher elevation; Antarctic Peninsula has the most moderate climate; higher temperatures occur in January along the coast and average slightly below freezing; summers characterized by continuous daylight, while winters bring continuous darkness; persistent high pressure over the interior brings dry, subsiding air that results in very little cloud cover
ATA.hazards_text: katabatic (gravity-driven) winds blow coastward from the high interior; frequent blizzards form near the foot of the plateau; cyclonic storms form over the ocean and move clockwise along the coast; large icebergs may calve from ice shelf. Volcanoes: volcanic activity on Deception Island and isolated areas of West Antarctica; other seismic activity rare and weak

ZWE.lowest_point: junction of the Runde and Save Rivers
ZWE.terrain: mostly high plateau with higher central plateau (high veld); mountains in east
ZWE.climate_text: tropical; moderated by altitude; rainy season (November to March)
ZWE.hazards_text: recurring droughts; floods and severe storms are rare

ZMB.terrain: mostly high plateau with some hills and mountains
ZMB.climate_text: tropical; modified by altitude; rainy season (October to April)
ZMB.hazards_text: periodic drought; tropical storms (November to April)

YEM.terrain: narrow coastal plain backed by flat-topped hills and rugged mountains; dissected upland desert plains in center slope into the desert interior of the Arabian Peninsula
YEM.climate_text: mostly desert; hot and humid along west coast; temperate in western mountains affected by seasonal monsoon; extraordinarily hot, dry, harsh desert in east
YEM.hazards_text: sandstorms and dust storms in summer. Volcanoes: limited volcanic activity; Jebel at Tair (Jabal al-Tair, Jebel Teir, Jabal al-Tayr, Jazirat at-Tair) (244 m), which forms an island in the Red Sea, became active in 2007; other historically active volcanoes include Harra of Arhab, Harras of Dhamar, Harra es-Sawad, and Jebel Zubair, although many of these have not erupted in over a century

VNM.terrain: low, flat delta in south and north; central highlands; hilly, mountainous in far north and northwest
VNM.climate_text: tropical in south; monsoonal in north with hot, rainy season (May to September) and warm, dry season (October to March)
VNM.hazards_text: occasional typhoons (May to January) with extensive flooding, especially in the Mekong River delta

VEN.terrain: Andes Mountains and Maracaibo Lowlands in northwest; central plains (llanos); Guiana Highlands in southeast
VEN.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; more moderate in highlands
VEN.hazards_text: subject to floods, rockslides, mudslides; periodic droughts

VAT.climate_text: temperate; mild, rainy winters (September to May) with hot, dry summers (May to September)

VUT.terrain: mostly mountainous islands of volcanic origin; narrow coastal plains
VUT.climate_text: tropical; moderated by southeast trade winds from May to October; moderate rainfall from November to April; may be affected by cyclones from December to April
VUT.hazards_text: tropical cyclones (January to April); volcanic activity; volcanism also causes minor earthquakes; tsunamis. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity with multiple eruptions in recent years; Yasur (361 m), one of the world's most active volcanoes, has experienced continuous activity in recent centuries; other historically active volcanoes include Aoba, Ambrym, Epi, Gaua, Kuwae, Lopevi, Suretamatai, and Traitor's Head

UZB.terrain: mostly flat-to-rolling sandy desert with dunes; broad, flat intensely irrigated river valleys along course of Amu Darya, Syr Darya (Sirdaryo), and Zaravshan; Fergana Valley in east surrounded by mountainous Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan; shrinking Aral Sea in west
UZB.climate_text: mostly mid-latitude desert, long, hot summers, mild winters; semiarid grassland in east
UZB.hazards_text: earthquakes; floods; landslides or mudslides; avalanches; droughts

URY.terrain: mostly rolling plains and low hills; fertile coastal lowland
URY.climate_text: warm temperate; freezing temperatures almost unknown
URY.hazards_text: seasonally high winds (the pampero is a chilly and occasional violent wind that blows north from the Argentine pampas), droughts, floods; because of the absence of mountains, which act as weather barriers, all locations are particularly vulnerable to rapid changes from weather fronts

FSM.quake_max_place: State of Yap, Federated States of Micronesia
FSM.terrain: islands vary geologically from high mountainous islands to low, coral atolls; volcanic outcroppings on Pohnpei, Kosrae, and Chuuk
FSM.climate_text: tropical; heavy year-round rainfall, especially in the eastern islands; located on southern edge of the typhoon belt with occasionally severe damage

MHL.terrain: low coral limestone and sand islands
MHL.climate_text: tropical; hot and humid; wet season May to November; islands border typhoon belt

MNP.terrain: the southern islands in this north-south trending archipelago are limestone, with fringing coral reefs; the northern islands are volcanic, with active volcanoes on several islands
MNP.climate_text: tropical marine; moderated by northeast trade winds, little seasonal temperature variation; dry season December to June, rainy season July to October
MNP.hazards_text: active volcanoes on Pagan and Agrihan; typhoons (especially August to November)

VIR.quake_max_place: near Saint Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands

GUM.terrain: volcanic origin, surrounded by coral reefs; relatively flat coralline limestone plateau (source of most fresh water), with steep coastal cliffs and narrow coastal plains in north, low hills in center, mountains in south
GUM.climate_text: tropical marine; generally warm and humid, moderated by northeast trade winds; dry season (January to June), rainy season (July to December); little seasonal temperature variation
GUM.hazards_text: frequent squalls during rainy season; relatively rare but potentially destructive typhoons (June to December)

ASM.terrain: five volcanic islands with rugged peaks and limited coastal plains, two coral atolls (Rose Atoll, Swains Island)
ASM.climate_text: tropical marine, moderated by southeast trade winds; annual rainfall averages about 3 m; rainy season (November to April), dry season (May to October); little seasonal temperature variation
ASM.hazards_text: cyclones common from December to March. Volcanoes: limited volcanic activity on the Ofu and Olosega Islands; neither has erupted since the 19th century

PRI.terrain: mostly mountains with coastal plain in north; precipitous mountains to the sea on west coast; sandy beaches along most coastal areas
PRI.climate_text: tropical marine, mild; little seasonal temperature variation

IOT.terrain: flat and low coral atolls (most areas do not exceed 2 m, or 6.6 ft, in elevation); sits atop the submarine volcanic Chagos-Laccadive Ridge
IOT.climate_text: tropical marine; hot, humid, moderated by trade winds
IOT.hazards_text: none; located outside routes of Indian Ocean cyclones

SHN.highest_point: Queen Mary's Peak on Tristan da Cunha
SHN.terrain: the islands of this group are of volcanic origin associated with the Atlantic Mid-Ocean Ridge Saint Helena: rugged, volcanic; small scattered plateaus and plains Ascension: surface covered by lava flows and cinder cones of 44 dormant volcanoes; terrain rises to the east Tristan da Cunha: sheer cliffs line the coastline of the nearly circular island; the flanks of the central volcanic peak are deeply dissected; narrow coastal plain lies between The Peak and the coastal cliffs
SHN.climate_text: Saint Helena: tropical marine; mild, tempered by trade winds Ascension Island: tropical marine; mild, semi-arid Tristan da Cunha: temperate marine; mild, tempered by trade winds (tends to be cooler than Saint Helena)
SHN.hazards_text: active volcanism. Volcanoes: the volcanoes of Tristan da Cunha (2,060 m) and Nightingale Island (365 m) are active

PCN.highest_point: Palwala Valley Point on Big Ridge
PCN.terrain: rugged volcanic formation; rocky coastline with cliffs
PCN.climate_text: tropical; hot and humid; modified by southeast trade winds; rainy season (November to March)
PCN.hazards_text: occasional tropical cyclones (especially November to March), but generally only heavy tropical storms; landslides

AIA.terrain: flat and low-lying island of coral and limestone
AIA.climate_text: tropical; moderated by northeast trade winds
AIA.hazards_text: frequent hurricanes and other tropical storms (July to October)

FLK.terrain: rocky, hilly, mountainous with some boggy, undulating plains
FLK.climate_text: cold marine; strong westerly winds, cloudy, humid; rain occurs on more than half of days in year; average annual rainfall is 60 cm in Stanley; occasional snow all year, except in January and February, but typically does not accumulate
FLK.hazards_text: strong winds persist throughout the year

CYM.highest_point: 1 km SW of The Bluff on Cayman Brac
CYM.terrain: low-lying limestone base surrounded by coral reefs
CYM.climate_text: tropical marine; warm, rainy summers (May to October) and cool, relatively dry winters (November to April)

BMU.terrain: low hills separated by fertile depressions
BMU.climate_text: subtropical; mild, humid; gales, strong winds common in winter

VGB.terrain: coral islands relatively flat; volcanic islands steep, hilly
VGB.climate_text: subtropical; humid; temperatures moderated by trade winds
VGB.hazards_text: hurricanes and tropical storms (July to October)

TCA.highest_point: Blue Hill on Providenciales and Flamingo Hill on East Caicos
TCA.terrain: low, flat limestone; extensive marshes and mangrove swamps
TCA.climate_text: tropical; marine; moderated by trade winds; sunny and relatively dry

MSR.highest_point: Soufriere Hills volcano pre-eruption height was
MSR.terrain: volcanic island, mostly mountainous, with small coastal lowland
MSR.climate_text: tropical; little daily or seasonal temperature variation
MSR.hazards_text: volcanic eruptions; severe hurricanes (June to November). Volcanoes: Soufrière Hills volcano (915 m) has erupted continuously since 1995; a massive eruption in 1997 destroyed most of the capital, Plymouth, and made about half of the island uninhabitable; the island of Montserrat is part of the volcanic island arc of the Lesser Antilles that extends from Saba in the north to Grenada in the south

JEY.terrain: gently rolling plain with low, rugged hills along north coast
JEY.climate_text: temperate; mild winters and cool summers
JEY.hazards_text: very large tidal variation can be hazardous to navigation

GGY.terrain: mostly flat with low hills in southwest
GGY.climate_text: temperate with mild winters and cool summers; about 50% of days are overcast
GGY.hazards_text: very large tidal variation and fast currents can make local waters dangerous

IMN.terrain: hills in north and south bisected by central valley
IMN.climate_text: temperate; cool summers and mild winters; overcast about a third of the time
IMN.hazards_text: occasional high winds and rough seas

GBR.terrain: mostly rugged hills and low mountains; level to rolling plains in east and southeast
GBR.climate_text: temperate; moderated by prevailing southwest winds over the North Atlantic Current; more than one-half of the days are overcast

ARE.terrain: flat, barren coastal plain merging into rolling sand dunes of vast desert; mountains in east

UKR.terrain: mostly fertile plains (steppes) and plateaus, with mountains found only in the west (the Carpathians) or in the extreme south of the Crimean Peninsula
UKR.climate_text: temperate continental; Mediterranean only on the southern Crimean coast; precipitation disproportionately distributed, highest in west and north, lesser in east and southeast; winters vary from cool along the Black Sea to cold farther inland; warm summers across the greater part of the country, hot in the south

UGA.terrain: mostly plateau with rim of mountains
UGA.climate_text: tropical; generally rainy with two dry seasons (December to February, June to August); semiarid in northeast

TKM.lowest_point: Vpadina Akchanaya (Sarygamysh Koli is a lake in northern Turkmenistan with a water level that fluctuates above and below the elevation of Vpadina Akchanaya, the lake has dropped as low as
TKM.terrain: flat-to-rolling sandy desert with dunes rising to mountains in the south; low mountains along border with Iran; borders Caspian Sea in west
TKM.hazards_text: earthquakes; mudslides; droughts; dust storms; floods

TUR.terrain: high central plateau (Anatolia); narrow coastal plain; several mountain ranges
TUR.climate_text: temperate; hot, dry summers with mild, wet winters; harsher in interior
TUR.hazards_text: severe earthquakes, especially in northern Turkey, along an arc extending from the Sea of Marmara to Lake Van; landslides; flooding. Volcanoes: limited volcanic activity; the three historically active volcanoes (Ararat, Nemrut Dagi, and Tendurek Dagi) have not erupted since the 19th century or earlier

TUN.terrain: mountains in north; hot, dry central plain; semiarid south merges into the Sahara
TUN.climate_text: temperate in north with mild, rainy winters and hot, dry summers; desert in south

TTO.quake_max_place: near Sangre Grande, Trinidad and Tobago
TTO.terrain: mostly plains with some hills and low mountains
TTO.hazards_text: outside usual path of hurricanes and other tropical storms

TON.terrain: mostly flat islands with limestone bedrock formed from uplifted coral formation; others have limestone overlying volcanic rock
TON.climate_text: tropical; modified by trade winds; warm season (December to May), cool season (May to December)
TON.hazards_text: cyclones (October to April); earthquakes and volcanic activity on Fonuafo'ou. Volcanoes: moderate volcanic activity; Fonualei (180 m) has had frequent activity in recent years, and Niuafo'ou (260 m) has forced evacuations; other historically active volcanoes include Late and Tofua

TGO.terrain: gently rolling savanna in north; central hills; southern plateau; low coastal plain with extensive lagoons and marshes
TGO.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid in south; semiarid in north
TGO.hazards_text: hot, dry harmattan wind can reduce visibility in north during winter; periodic droughts

TLS.lowest_point: Timor Sea, Savu Sea, and Banda Sea
TLS.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; distinct rainy and dry seasons
TLS.hazards_text: floods and landslides are common; earthquakes; tsunamis; tropical cyclones

THA.terrain: central plain; Khorat Plateau in the east; mountains elsewhere
THA.climate_text: tropical; rainy, warm, cloudy southwest monsoon (mid-May to September); dry, cool northeast monsoon (November to mid-March); southern isthmus always hot and humid
THA.hazards_text: land subsidence in Bangkok area resulting from the depletion of the water table; droughts

TZA.terrain: plains along coast; central plateau; highlands in north, south
TZA.climate_text: varies from tropical along coast to temperate in highlands
TZA.hazards_text: flooding on the central plateau during the rainy season; drought. Volcanoes: limited volcanic activity; Ol Doinyo Lengai (2,962 m) has emitted lava in recent years; other historically active volcanoes include Kieyo and Meru

TWN.terrain: eastern two-thirds mostly rugged mountains; flat to gently rolling plains in west
TWN.climate_text: tropical; marine; rainy season during southwest monsoon (June to August); persistent and extensive cloudiness all year
TWN.hazards_text: earthquakes; typhoons. Volcanoes: Kueishantao Island (401 m), east of Taiwan, is the only historically active volcano, but it has not erupted in centuries

SYR.terrain: primarily semiarid and desert plateau; narrow coastal plain; mountains in west
SYR.climate_text: mostly desert; hot, dry, sunny summers (June to August) and mild, rainy winters (December to February) along coast; cold weather with snow or sleet periodically in Damascus
SYR.hazards_text: dust storms, sandstorms. Volcanoes: Syria's two historically active volcanoes, Es Safa and an unnamed volcano near the Turkish border, have not erupted in centuries

SWZ.terrain: mostly mountains and hills; some moderately sloping plains
SWZ.climate_text: varies from tropical to near temperate

SUR.lowest_point: unnamed location in the coastal plain
SUR.terrain: mostly rolling hills; narrow coastal plain with swamps
lakes: Professor Doctor Ingenieur W. J. Van Blommestein Meer

SSD.terrain: plains in the north and center rise to southern highlands along the border with Uganda and Kenya; the White Nile, flowing north out of the uplands of Central Africa, is the major geographic feature of the country; The Sudd (a name derived from floating vegetation that hinders navigation) is a large swampy area of more than 100,000 sq km fed by the waters of the White Nile that dominates the center of the country
SSD.climate_text: hot with seasonal rainfall influenced by the annual shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone; rainfall heaviest in upland areas of the south and diminishes to the north

SDN.terrain: generally flat, featureless plain; desert dominates the north
SDN.climate_text: hot and dry; arid desert; rainy season varies by region (April to November)
SDN.hazards_text: dust storms and periodic persistent droughts

LKA.terrain: mostly low, flat to rolling plain; mountains in south-central interior
LKA.climate_text: tropical monsoon; northeast monsoon (December to March); southwest monsoon (June to October)

ESP.highest_point: Pico de Teide on Canary Islands
ESP.terrain: large, flat to dissected plateau surrounded by rugged hills; Pyrenees Mountains in north
ESP.climate_text: temperate; clear, hot summers in interior, more moderate and cloudy along coast; cloudy, cold winters in interior, partly cloudy and cool along coast
ESP.hazards_text: periodic droughts, occasional flooding. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the Canary Islands, located off Africa's northwest coast; Teide (3,715 m) has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; La Palma (2,426 m) is the most active of the Canary Islands volcanoes; Lanzarote is the only other historically active volcano

KOR.terrain: mostly hills and mountains; wide coastal plains in west and south
KOR.climate_text: temperate, with rainfall heavier in summer than winter; cold winters
KOR.hazards_text: occasional typhoons bring high winds and floods; low-level seismic activity common in southwest. Volcanoes: Halla (1,950 m) is considered historically active; it has not erupted in many centuries

ZAF.terrain: vast interior plateau rimmed by rugged hills and narrow coastal plain
ZAF.climate_text: mostly semiarid; subtropical along east coast; sunny days, cool nights
ZAF.hazards_text: prolonged droughts. Volcanoes: the volcano that formed Marion Island in the Prince Edward Islands is South Africa's only active volcano

SOM.terrain: mostly flat to undulating plateau rising to hills in north
SOM.climate_text: principally desert; northeast monsoon (December to February), moderate temperatures in north and hot in south; southwest monsoon (May to October), torrid in the north and hot in the south, irregular rainfall, hot and humid periods (tangambili) between monsoons
SOM.hazards_text: recurring droughts; frequent dust storms over eastern plains in summer; floods during rainy season

SLB.terrain: mostly rugged mountains with some low coral atolls
SLB.climate_text: tropical monsoon; few temperature and weather extremes
SLB.hazards_text: tropical cyclones, but rarely destructive; geologically active region with frequent earthquakes, tremors, and volcanic activity; tsunamis. Volcanoes: Tinakula (851 m) has frequent eruption activity, and an eruption of Savo (485 m) could affect the capital Honiara on nearby Guadalcanal

SVK.terrain: rugged mountains in the central and northern part and lowlands in the south
SVK.climate_text: temperate; cool summers; cold, cloudy, humid winters

SVN.terrain: a short southwestern coastal strip of Karst topography on the Adriatic; an alpine mountain region lies adjacent to Italy and Austria in the north; mixed mountains and valleys with numerous rivers to the east
SVN.climate_text: Mediterranean climate on the coast, continental climate with mild to hot summers and cold winters in the plateaus and valleys to the east

SGP.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid, rainy; two distinct monsoon seasons - northeastern monsoon (December to March) and southwestern monsoon (June to September); inter-monsoon - frequent afternoon and early evening thunderstorms

SLE.terrain: coastal belt of mangrove swamps, wooded hill country, upland plateau, mountains in east
SLE.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; summer rainy season (May to December); winter dry season (December to April)
SLE.hazards_text: dry, sand-laden harmattan winds blow from the Sahara (December to February); sandstorms, dust storms

SYC.terrain: Mahe Group is volcanic with a narrow coastal strip and rocky, hilly interior; others are relatively flat coral atolls, or elevated reefs; sits atop the submarine Mascarene Plateau
SYC.climate_text: tropical marine; humid; cooler season during southeast monsoon (late May to September); warmer season during northwest monsoon (March to May)
SYC.hazards_text: lies outside the cyclone belt, so severe storms are rare; occasional short droughts

SRB.terrain: extremely varied; to the north, rich fertile plains; to the east, limestone ranges and basins; to the southeast, ancient mountains and hills
SRB.climate_text: in the north, continental climate (cold winters and hot, humid summers with well-distributed rainfall); in other parts, continental and Mediterranean climate (relatively cold winters with heavy snowfall and hot, dry summers and autumns)

SEN.highest_point: unnamed elevation 2.8 km southeast of Nepen Diaka
SEN.terrain: generally low, rolling, plains rising to foothills in southeast
SEN.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; rainy season (May to November) has strong southeast winds; dry season (December to April) dominated by hot, dry, harmattan wind

SAU.climate_text: harsh, dry desert with great temperature extremes
SAU.hazards_text: frequent sand and dust storms. Volcanoes: little activity in the past few centuries, despite many volcanic formations; volcanoes include Harrat Rahat, Harrat Khaybar, Harrat Lunayyir, and Jabal Yar

STP.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; one rainy season (October to May)

SMR.climate_text: Mediterranean; mild to cool winters; warm, sunny summers

WSM.terrain: two main islands (Savaii, Upolu) and several smaller islands and uninhabited islets; narrow coastal plain with volcanic, rugged mountains in interior
WSM.climate_text: tropical; rainy season (November to April), dry season (May to October)
WSM.hazards_text: occasional cyclones; active volcanism. Volcanoes: Savai'I Island (1,858 m) is historically active

VCT.quake_max_place: near Barrouallie, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
VCT.climate_text: tropical; little seasonal temperature variation; rainy season (May to November)
VCT.hazards_text: hurricanes; La Soufrière volcano on the island of Saint Vincent is a constant threat. Volcanoes: La Soufrière (1,234 m) last erupted in 1979; the island of Saint Vincent is part of the volcanic-island arc of the Lesser Antilles that extends from Saba in the north to Grenada in the south

LCA.terrain: volcanic and mountainous with broad, fertile valleys
LCA.climate_text: tropical, moderated by northeast trade winds; dry season January to April, rainy season May to August
LCA.hazards_text: hurricanes. Volcanoes: Mount Gimie (948 m), also known as Qualibou, is a caldera on the west of the island; the iconic twin pyramidal peaks of Gros Piton (771 m) and Petit Piton (743 m) are lava-dome remnants associated with the Soufrière volcano; there have been no historical magmatic eruptions, but a minor steam eruption in 1766 spread a thin layer of ash over a wide area; Saint Lucia is part of the volcanic-island arc of the Lesser Antilles that extends from Saba in the north to Grenada in the south

KNA.quake_max_place: near Market Shop, Saint Kitts and Nevis
KNA.climate_text: tropical, tempered by constant sea breezes; little seasonal temperature variation; rainy season (May to November)
KNA.hazards_text: hurricanes (July to October). Volcanoes: Mount Liamuiga (1,156 m) on Saint Kitts and Nevis Peak (985 m) on Nevis are part of the volcanic-island arc of the Lesser Antilles, which extends from Saba in the north to Grenada in the south

RWA.terrain: mostly grassy uplands and hills; relief is mountainous with altitude declining from west to east
RWA.climate_text: temperate; two rainy seasons (February to April, November to January); mild in mountains with frost and snow possible
RWA.hazards_text: periodic droughts; the volcanic Virunga Mountains are in the northwest along the border with Democratic Republic of the Congo. Volcanoes: Visoke (3,711 m), on the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, is the country's only historically active volcano

ROU.terrain: central Transylvanian Basin is separated from the Moldavian Plateau on the east by the Eastern Carpathian Mountains and separated from the Walachian Plain on the south by the Transylvanian Alps
ROU.climate_text: temperate; cold, cloudy winters with frequent snow and fog; sunny summers with frequent showers and thunderstorms
ROU.hazards_text: earthquakes, most severe in south and southwest; geologic structure and climate promote landslides

QAT.climate_text: arid; mild, pleasant winters; very hot, humid summers

PRT.highest_point: Ponta do Pico on Ilha do Pico in the Azores
PRT.terrain: the west-flowing Tagus River divides the country: the north is mountainous toward the interior, while the south is characterized by rolling plains
PRT.climate_text: maritime temperate; cool and rainy in north, warmer and drier in south
PRT.hazards_text: Azores subject to severe earthquakes. Volcanoes: limited volcanic activity in the Azores Islands; Fayal or Faial (1,043 m) last erupted in 1958; most volcanoes have not erupted in centuries; historically active volcanoes include Agua de Pau, Furnas, Pico, Picos Volcanic System, San Jorge, Sete Cidades, and Terceira

POL.terrain: mostly flat plain; mountains along southern border
POL.climate_text: temperate with cold, cloudy, moderately severe winters with frequent precipitation; mild summers with frequent showers and thundershowers

PHL.terrain: mostly mountains with narrow to extensive coastal lowlands
PHL.climate_text: tropical marine; northeast monsoon (November to April); southwest monsoon (May to October)
PHL.hazards_text: astride typhoon belt, usually affected by several cyclonic storms each year; landslides; active volcanoes; destructive earthquakes; tsunamis. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity; Taal (311 m) has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Mayon (2,462 m), the country's most active volcano, erupted in 2009 and forced over 33,000 to be evacuated; other historically active volcanoes include Biliran, Babuyan Claro, Bulusan, Camiguin, Camiguin de Babuyanes, Didicas, Iraya, Jolo, Kanlaon, Makaturing, Musuan, Parker, Pinatubo, and Ragang; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

PRY.lowest_point: junction of Río Paraguay and Río Paraná
PRY.terrain: grassy plains and wooded hills east of Rio Paraguay; Gran Chaco region west of Rio Paraguay mostly low, marshy plain near the river, and dry forest and thorny scrub elsewhere
PRY.climate_text: subtropical to temperate; substantial rainfall in the eastern portions, becoming semiarid in the far west
PRY.hazards_text: local flooding in southeast (early September to June); poorly drained plains may become boggy (early October to June)

PNG.terrain: small, flat islands, islets, cays, and reefs
PNG.hazards_text: typhoons; numerous reefs and shoals pose a serious maritime hazard

PAN.terrain: interior mostly steep, rugged mountains with dissected, upland plains; coastal plains with rolling hills
PAN.climate_text: tropical maritime; hot, humid, cloudy; prolonged rainy season (May to January), short dry season (January to May)
PAN.hazards_text: occasional severe storms and forest fires in the Darien area

PLW.terrain: varying topography from the high, mountainous main island of Babelthuap to low, coral islands usually fringed by large barrier reefs
PLW.climate_text: tropical; hot and humid; wet season May to November

OMN.terrain: central desert plain, rugged mountains in north and south
OMN.climate_text: dry desert; hot, humid along coast; hot, dry interior; strong southwest summer monsoon (May to September) in far south
OMN.hazards_text: summer winds often raise large sandstorms and dust storms in interior; periodic droughts

PRK.terrain: mostly hills and mountains separated by deep, narrow valleys; wide coastal plains in west, discontinuous in east
PRK.climate_text: temperate, with rainfall concentrated in summer; long, bitter winters
PRK.hazards_text: late spring droughts often followed by severe flooding; occasional typhoons during the early fall. Volcanoes: P'aektu-san (2,744 m) (also known as Baitoushan, Baegdu, or Changbaishan), on the Chinese border, is considered historically active

NGA.terrain: southern lowlands merge into central hills and plateaus; mountains in southeast, plains in north
NGA.climate_text: varies; equatorial in south, tropical in center, arid in north

NER.terrain: predominately desert plains and sand dunes; flat to rolling plains in south; hills in north
NER.climate_text: desert; mostly hot, dry, dusty; tropical in extreme south

NIC.terrain: extensive Atlantic coastal plains rising to central interior mountains; narrow Pacific coastal plain interrupted by volcanoes
NIC.climate_text: tropical in lowlands, cooler in highlands
NIC.hazards_text: destructive earthquakes; volcanoes; landslides; extremely susceptible to hurricanes. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity; Cerro Negro (728 m) is one of Nicaragua's most active volcanoes; its lava flows and ash have been known to cause significant damage to farmland and buildings; other historically active volcanoes include Concepcion, Cosiguina, Las Pilas, Masaya, Momotombo, San Cristobal, and Telica

NIU.highest_point: unnamed elevation 1.4 km east of Hikutavake
NIU.terrain: steep limestone cliffs along coast, central plateau
NIU.climate_text: tropical; modified by southeast trade winds

COK.terrain: low coral atolls in north; volcanic, hilly islands in south
COK.climate_text: tropical oceanic; moderated by trade winds; a dry season from April to November and a more humid season from December to March

NLD.terrain: mostly coastal lowland and reclaimed land (polders); some hills in southeast
NLD.climate_text: temperate; marine; cool summers and mild winters
NLD.hazards_text: flooding. Volcanoes: Mount Scenery (887 m), located on the island of Saba in the Caribbean, last erupted in 1640; Round Hill (601 m), a dormant volcano also known as "The Quill," is located on the island of St. Eustatius in the Caribbean; these islands are at the northern end of the volcanic island arc of the Lesser Antilles that extends south to Grenada

ABW.terrain: flat with a few hills; scant vegetation
ABW.climate_text: tropical marine; little seasonal temperature variation
ABW.hazards_text: hurricanes; lies outside the Caribbean hurricane belt and is rarely threatened

CUW.climate_text: tropical marine climate, ameliorated by northeast trade winds, results in mild temperatures; semiarid with average rainfall of 60 cm/year
CUW.hazards_text: Curacao is south of the Caribbean hurricane belt and is rarely threatened

NRU.terrain: sandy beach rises to fertile ring around raised coral reefs with phosphate plateau in center
NRU.climate_text: tropical with a monsoonal pattern; rainy season (November to February)

NAM.terrain: mostly high plateau; Namib Desert along coast; Kalahari Desert in east
NAM.climate_text: desert; hot, dry; rainfall sparse and erratic

MOZ.terrain: mostly coastal lowlands, uplands in center, high plateaus in northwest, mountains in west
MOZ.hazards_text: severe droughts; devastating cyclones and floods in central and southern provinces

MAR.terrain: mountainous northern coast (Rif Mountains) and interior (Atlas Mountains) bordered by large plateaus with intermontane valleys, and fertile coastal plains; the south is mostly low, flat desert with large areas of rocky or sandy surfaces
MAR.climate_text: Mediterranean in the north, becoming more extreme in the interior; in the south, hot, dry desert; rain is rare; cold offshore air currents produce fog and heavy dew
MAR.hazards_text: in the north, the mountains are geologically unstable and subject to earthquakes; periodic droughts; windstorms; flash floods; landslides; in the south, a hot, dry, dust/sand-laden sirocco wind can occur during winter and spring; widespread harmattan haze exists 60% of time, often severely restricting visibility

ESH.terrain: mostly low, flat desert with large areas of rocky or sandy surfaces rising to small mountains in south and northeast
ESH.climate_text: hot, dry desert; rain is rare; cold offshore air currents produce fog and heavy dew
ESH.hazards_text: hot, dry, dust/sand-laden sirocco wind can occur during winter and spring; widespread harmattan haze exists 60% of time, often severely restricting visibility

MNE.terrain: highly indented coastline with narrow coastal plain backed by rugged high limestone mountains and plateaus
MNE.climate_text: Mediterranean climate, hot dry summers and autumns and relatively cold winters with heavy snowfalls inland

MNG.terrain: vast semidesert and desert plains, grassy steppe, mountains in west and southwest; Gobi Desert in south-central
MNG.climate_text: desert; continental (large daily and seasonal temperature ranges)
MNG.hazards_text: dust storms; grassland and forest fires; drought; "zud," which is harsh winter conditions

MDA.terrain: rolling steppe, gradual slope south to Black Sea

MCO.highest_point: Chemin des Revoires on Mont Agel
MCO.climate_text: Mediterranean with mild, wet winters and hot, dry summers

MEX.terrain: high, rugged mountains; low coastal plains; high plateaus; desert
MEX.hazards_text: tsunamis along the Pacific coast; volcanoes and destructive earthquakes in the center and south; hurricanes on the Pacific, Gulf of America, and Caribbean coasts. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the central-southern part of the country; the volcanoes in Baja California are mostly dormant; Colima (3,850 m) is Mexico's most active volcano and is responsible for periodic evacuations of nearby villagers; it has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Popocatepetl (5,426 m) poses a threat to Mexico City; other historically active volcanoes include Barcena, Ceboruco, El Chichon, Michoacan-Guanajuato, Pico de Orizaba, San Martin, Socorro, and Tacana; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

MUS.terrain: small coastal plain rising to discontinuous mountains encircling central plateau
MUS.climate_text: tropical, modified by southeast trade winds; warm, dry winter (May to November); hot, wet, humid summer (November to May)
MUS.hazards_text: cyclones (November to April); almost completely surrounded by reefs that may pose maritime hazards

MRT.terrain: mostly barren, flat plains of the Sahara; some central hills
MRT.hazards_text: hot, dry, dust/sand-laden sirocco wind primarily in March and April; periodic droughts

MLT.terrain: mostly low, rocky, flat to dissected plains; many coastal cliffs
MLT.climate_text: Mediterranean; mild, rainy winters; hot, dry summers

MLI.terrain: mostly flat to rolling northern plains covered by sand; savanna in south, rugged hills in northeast
MLI.climate_text: subtropical to arid; hot and dry (February to June); rainy, humid, and mild (June to November); cool and dry (November to February)
MLI.hazards_text: hot, dust-laden harmattan haze common during dry seasons; recurring droughts; occasional Niger River flooding

MDV.terrain: flat coral atolls, with white sandy beaches; sits atop the submarine volcanic Chagos-Laccadive Ridge
MDV.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; dry, northeast monsoon (November to March); rainy, southwest monsoon (June to August)
MDV.hazards_text: tsunamis; low elevation of islands makes them sensitive to sea level rise

MYS.terrain: coastal plains rising to hills and mountains
MYS.climate_text: tropical; annual southwest (April to October) and northeast (October to February) monsoons

MWI.lowest_point: junction of the Shire River and international boundary with Mozambique
MWI.terrain: narrow elongated plateau with rolling plains, rounded hills, some mountains
MWI.climate_text: sub-tropical; rainy season (November to May); dry season (May to November)

MDG.terrain: narrow coastal plain, high plateau and mountains in center
MDG.climate_text: tropical along coast, temperate inland, arid in south
MDG.hazards_text: periodic cyclones; drought; and locust infestation. Volcanoes: Madagascar's volcanoes have not erupted in recorded history

MKD.terrain: mountainous with deep basins and valleys; three large lakes, each divided by a frontier line; country bisected by the Vardar River
MKD.climate_text: warm, dry summers and autumns; relatively cold winters with heavy snowfall

LUX.terrain: mostly gently rolling uplands with broad, shallow valleys; uplands to slightly mountainous in the north; steep slope down to Moselle flood plain in the southeast
LUX.climate_text: modified continental with mild winters, cool summers

LTU.terrain: lowland, many scattered small lakes, fertile soil
LTU.climate_text: transitional, between maritime and continental; wet, moderate winters and summers

LIE.terrain: mostly mountainous (Alps) with Rhine Valley in western third
LIE.climate_text: continental; cold, cloudy winters with frequent snow or rain; cool to moderately warm, cloudy, humid summers

LBY.terrain: mostly barren, flat to undulating plains, plateaus, depressions
LBY.climate_text: Mediterranean along coast; dry, extreme desert interior
LBY.hazards_text: hot, dry, dust-laden ghibli is a southern wind lasting one to four days in spring and fall; dust storms, sandstorms

LBR.terrain: mostly flat to rolling coastal plains rising to rolling plateau and low mountains in northeast
LBR.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; dry winters with hot days and cool to cold nights; wet, cloudy summers with frequent heavy showers
LBR.hazards_text: dust-laden harmattan winds blow from the Sahara (December to March)

LSO.lowest_point: junction of the Orange and Makhaleng Rivers
LSO.terrain: mostly highland with plateaus, hills, and mountains
LSO.climate_text: temperate; cool to cold, dry winters; hot, wet summers

LBN.terrain: narrow coastal plain; El Beqaa (Bekaa Valley) separates Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon Mountains
LBN.climate_text: Mediterranean; mild to cool, wet winters with hot, dry summers; the Lebanon Mountains experience heavy winter snows

LVA.hazards_text: large percentage of agricultural fields can become waterlogged and require drainage

LAO.terrain: mostly rugged mountains; some plains and plateaus
LAO.climate_text: tropical monsoon; rainy season (May to November); dry season (December to April)

KWT.highest_point: 3.6 km W. of Al-Salmi Border Post
KWT.terrain: flat to slightly undulating desert plain
KWT.climate_text: dry desert; intensely hot summers; short, cool winters
KWT.hazards_text: sudden cloudbursts are common from October to April and bring heavy rain, which can damage roads and houses; sandstorms and dust storms occur throughout the year but are most common between March and August

UNK.terrain: flat fluvial basin at an elevation of 400-700 m above sea level surrounded by several high mountain ranges with elevations of 2,000 to 2,500 m
UNK.climate_text: influenced by continental air masses resulting in relatively cold winters with heavy snowfall and hot, dry summers and autumns; Mediterranean and alpine influences create regional variation; maximum rainfall between October and December

KIR.terrain: mostly low-lying coral atolls surrounded by extensive reefs
KIR.climate_text: tropical; marine, hot and humid, moderated by trade winds
KIR.hazards_text: typhoons can occur any time, but usually November to March; occasional tornadoes; low level of some of the islands make them sensitive to changes in sea level

KEN.terrain: low plains rise to central highlands bisected by Great Rift Valley; fertile plateau in west
KEN.climate_text: varies from tropical along coast to arid in interior
KEN.hazards_text: recurring drought; flooding during rainy seasons. Volcanoes: limited volcanic activity; the Barrier (1,032 m) last erupted in 1921; South Island is the only other historically active volcano

JOR.terrain: mostly arid desert plateau; a great north-south geological rift along the west of the country is the dominant topographical feature and includes the Jordan River Valley, the Dead Sea, and the Jordanian Highlands
JOR.climate_text: mostly arid desert; rainy season in west (November to April)

JPN.climate_text: varies from tropical in south to cool temperate in north
JPN.hazards_text: many dormant and some active volcanoes; about 1,500 seismic occurrences (mostly tremors but occasional severe earthquakes) every year; tsunamis; typhoons. Volcanoes: both Unzen (1,500 m) and Sakura-jima (1,117 m), which lies near the densely populated city of Kagoshima, have been deemed Decade Volcanoes by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to their explosive history and close proximity to human populations; other notable historically active volcanoes include Asama (Honshu Island's most active volcano), Aso, Bandai, Fuji, Iwo-Jima, Kikai, Kirishima, Komaga-take, Oshima, Suwanosejima, Tokachi, Yake-dake, and Usu; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

JAM.terrain: mostly mountains, with narrow, discontinuous coastal plain

ISR.terrain: Negev desert in the south; low coastal plain; central mountains; Jordan Rift Valley
ISR.climate_text: temperate; hot and dry in southern and eastern desert areas
ISR.hazards_text: sandstorms may occur during spring and summer; droughts; periodic earthquakes

PSE.terrain: mostly rugged, dissected upland in west, flat plains descending to Jordan River Valley to the east
PSE.climate_text: temperate; temperature and precipitation vary with altitude, warm to hot summers, cool to mild winters

IRL.terrain: mostly flat to rolling interior plain surrounded by rugged hills and low mountains; sea cliffs on west coast
IRL.climate_text: temperate maritime; modified by North Atlantic Current; mild winters, cool summers; consistently humid; overcast about half the time

IRQ.terrain: mostly broad plains; reedy marshes along Iranian border in south with large flooded areas; mountains along borders with Iran and Turkey
IRQ.climate_text: mostly desert; mild to cool winters with dry, hot, cloudless summers; northern mountainous regions along Iranian and Turkish borders experience cold winters with occasionally heavy snows that melt in early spring, sometimes causing extensive flooding in central and southern Iraq

IRN.terrain: rugged, mountainous rim; high, central basin with deserts, mountains; small, discontinuous plains along both coasts
IRN.climate_text: mostly arid or semiarid, subtropical along Caspian coast
IRN.hazards_text: periodic droughts, floods; dust storms, sandstorms; earthquakes

IDN.terrain: mostly coastal lowlands; larger islands have interior mountains
IDN.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid; more moderate in highlands
IDN.hazards_text: occasional floods; severe droughts; tsunamis; earthquakes; volcanoes; forest fires. Volcanoes: Indonesia contains the most volcanoes of any country in the world, with over 75 historically active; significant volcanic activity occurs on Java, Sumatra, the Sunda Islands, Halmahera Island, Sulawesi Island, Sangihe Island, and in the Banda Sea; Merapi (2,968 m), Indonesia's most active volcano, has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; in 2018, a large explosion and flank collapse destroyed most of the island of Anak Krakatau (Child of Krakatau) and generated a deadly tsunami that left more than 400 dead; other notable historically active volcanoes include Agung, Awu, Karangetang, Krakatau (Krakatoa), Makian, Raung, Sinabung, and Tambora; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

HUN.terrain: mostly flat to rolling plains; hills and low mountains on the Slovakian border
HUN.climate_text: temperate; cold, cloudy, humid winters; warm summers

HND.terrain: mostly mountains in interior, narrow coastal plains
HND.climate_text: subtropical in lowlands, temperate in mountains
HND.hazards_text: frequent, but generally mild, earthquakes; extremely susceptible to damaging hurricanes and floods along the Caribbean coast

HTI.climate_text: tropical; semiarid where mountains in east cut off trade winds
HTI.hazards_text: lies in the middle of the hurricane belt and subject to severe storms from June to October; occasional flooding and earthquakes; periodic droughts

GUY.highest_point: Laberintos del Norte on Mount Roraima
GUY.terrain: mostly rolling highlands; low coastal plain; savanna in south
GUY.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid, moderated by northeast trade winds; two rainy seasons (May to August, November to January)
GUY.hazards_text: flash flood threat during rainy seasons

GNB.terrain: mostly low-lying coastal plain with a deeply indented estuarine coastline rising to savanna in east; numerous off-shore islands including the Arquipelago Dos Bijagos consisting of 18 main islands and many small islets
GNB.climate_text: tropical; generally hot and humid; monsoonal-type rainy season (June to November) with southwesterly winds; dry season (December to May) with northeasterly harmattan winds
GNB.hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan haze may reduce visibility during dry season; brush fires

GIN.terrain: generally flat coastal plain, hilly to mountainous interior
GIN.climate_text: generally hot and humid; monsoonal-type rainy season (June to November) with southwesterly winds; dry season (December to May) with northeasterly harmattan winds
GIN.hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan haze may reduce visibility during dry season

GTM.terrain: two east-west trending mountain chains divide the country into three regions: the mountainous highlands, the Pacific coast south of mountains, and the vast northern Peten lowlands
GTM.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid in lowlands; cooler in highlands
GTM.hazards_text: numerous volcanoes in mountains, with occasional violent earthquakes; Caribbean coast extremely susceptible to hurricanes and other tropical storms. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity in the Sierra Madre range; Santa Maria (3,772 m) has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Pacaya (2,552 m) is one of the country's most active volcanoes, with frequent eruptions since 1965; other historically active volcanoes include Acatenango, Almolonga, Atitlan, Fuego, and Tacana; see note 2 under "Geography - note"

GRD.terrain: volcanic in origin with central mountains
GRD.climate_text: tropical; tempered by northeast trade winds
GRD.hazards_text: lies on edge of hurricane belt; hurricane season lasts from June to November. Volcanoes: Mount Saint Catherine (840 m) is on the island of Grenada; Kick 'em Jenny, an active submarine volcano (seamount) on the Caribbean Sea floor, lies about 8 km (5 mi) north of Grenada; these two volcanoes are at the southern end of the volcanic island arc of the Lesser Antilles that extends to the Dutch dependency of Saba in the north

GRC.terrain: mountainous with ranges extending into the sea as peninsulas or chains of islands
GRC.climate_text: temperate; mild, wet winters; hot, dry summers
GRC.hazards_text: severe earthquakes. Volcanoes: Santorini (367 m) has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Methana and Nisyros in the Aegean are also classified as historically active

GHA.terrain: mostly low plains with dissected plateau in south-central area
GHA.climate_text: tropical; warm and comparatively dry along southeast coast; hot and humid in southwest; hot and dry in north
GHA.hazards_text: dry, dusty, northeastern harmattan winds from January to March; droughts

DEU.terrain: lowlands in north, uplands in center, Bavarian Alps in south
DEU.climate_text: temperate and marine; cool, cloudy, wet winters and summers; occasional warm mountain (foehn) wind

GMB.terrain: flood plain of the Gambia River flanked by some low hills
GMB.climate_text: tropical; hot, rainy season (June to November); cooler, dry season (November to May)

GAB.terrain: narrow coastal plain; hilly interior; savanna in east and south

FRA.terrain: metropolitan France: mostly flat plains or gently rolling hills in north and west; remainder is mountainous, especially Pyrenees in south, Alps in east French Guiana: low-lying coastal plains rising to hills and small mountains Guadeloupe: Basse-Terre is volcanic in origin with interior mountains; Grande-Terre is low limestone formation; most of the seven other islands are volcanic in origin Martinique: mountainous with indented coastline; dormant volcano Mayotte: generally undulating, with deep ravines and ancient volcanic peaks Reunion: mostly rugged and mountainous; fertile lowlands along coast
FRA.climate_text: metropolitan France: generally cool winters and mild summers, but mild winters and hot summers along the Mediterranean; occasional strong, cold, dry, north-to-northwesterly wind known as the mistral
FRA.hazards_text: metropolitan France: flooding; avalanches; midwinter windstorms; drought; forest fires in south overseas departments: hurricanes (cyclones); flooding. Volcanoes: Montagne Pelée (1,394 m) on the island of Martinique in the Caribbean is the most active volcano of the Lesser Antilles arc, although it last erupted in 1932; a catastrophic eruption in 1902 destroyed the city of St. Pierre, killing an estimated 30,000 people; La Soufrière (1,467 m) on the island of Guadeloupe has also had explosive eruptions in recent years

SPM.climate_text: cold and wet, with considerable mist and fog; spring and autumn are often windy
SPM.hazards_text: persistent fog throughout the year can be a maritime hazard

WLF.climate_text: tropical; hot, rainy season (November to April); cool, dry season (May to October); rains 250-300 cm per year (80% humidity); average temperature 26.6 degrees Celsius

MAF.climate_text: temperature averages 27-29 degrees Celsius all year long; low humidity, gentle trade winds, brief, intense rain showers; hurricane season stretches from July to November
MAF.hazards_text: subject to hurricanes from July to November

BLM.terrain: hilly, almost completely surrounded by shallow-water reefs, with plentiful beaches
BLM.climate_text: tropical, with practically no variation in temperature; has two seasons (dry and humid)

PYF.terrain: mixture of rugged high islands and low islands with reefs

NCL.climate_text: tropical; modified by southeast trade winds; hot, humid
NCL.hazards_text: cyclones, most frequent from November to March. Volcanoes: Matthew and Hunter Islands are historically active

ALA.climate_text: temperate; Mediterranean with hot, dry summers and cool winters

FIN.terrain: mostly low, flat to rolling plains interspersed with lakes and low hills
FIN.climate_text: cold temperate; potentially subarctic but comparatively mild because of moderating influence of the North Atlantic Current, Baltic Sea, and more than 60,000 lakes

FJI.climate_text: tropical marine; only slight seasonal temperature variation
FJI.hazards_text: cyclonic storms can occur from November to January

ETH.terrain: high plateau with central mountain range divided by Great Rift Valley
ETH.climate_text: tropical monsoon with wide topographic-induced variation
ETH.hazards_text: geologically active Great Rift Valley susceptible to earthquakes, volcanic eruptions; frequent droughts. Volcanoes: volcanic activity in the Great Rift Valley; Erta Ale (613 m) is the country's most active volcano; Dabbahu became active in 2005, forcing evacuations; other historically active volcanoes include Alayta, Dalaffilla, Dallol, Dama Ali, Fentale, Kone, Manda Hararo, and Manda-Inakir

EST.terrain: marshy, lowlands; flat in the north, hilly in the south
EST.climate_text: maritime; wet, moderate winters, cool summers
EST.hazards_text: sometimes flooding occurs in the spring

ERI.lowest_point: near Kulul within the Danakil Depression
ERI.terrain: dominated by extension of Ethiopian north-south trending highlands, descending on the east to a coastal desert plain, on the northwest to hilly terrain and on the southwest to flat-to-rolling plains
ERI.climate_text: hot, dry desert strip along Red Sea coast; cooler and wetter in the central highlands (up to 61 cm of rainfall annually, heaviest June to September); semiarid in western hills and lowlands
ERI.hazards_text: frequent droughts, rare earthquakes and volcanoes; locust swarms. Volcanoes: Dubbi (1,625 m), which last erupted in 1861, was the country's only historically active volcano until Nabro (2,218 m) came to life in 2011

GNQ.terrain: coastal plains rise to interior hills; islands are volcanic
GNQ.hazards_text: violent windstorms; flash floods. Volcanoes: Santa Isabel (3,007 m), which last erupted in 1923, is the country's only historically active volcano; Santa Isabel and two dormant volcanoes form Bioko Island in the Gulf of Guinea

SLV.terrain: mostly mountains with narrow coastal belt and central plateau
SLV.climate_text: tropical; rainy season (May to October); dry season (November to April); tropical on coast; temperate in uplands
SLV.hazards_text: known as the Land of Volcanoes; frequent and sometimes destructive earthquakes and volcanic activity; extremely susceptible to hurricanes. Volcanoes: significant volcanic activity; San Salvador (1,893 m), which last erupted in 1917, has the potential to cause major harm to the country's capital, which lies just below the volcano's slopes; San Miguel (2,130 m) is one of the most active volcanoes in the country; other historically active volcanoes include Conchaguita, Ilopango, Izalco, and Santa Ana

EGY.terrain: vast desert plateau interrupted by Nile valley and delta
EGY.climate_text: desert; hot, dry summers with moderate winters
EGY.hazards_text: periodic droughts; frequent earthquakes; flash floods; landslides; hot, driving windstorms called khamsin occur in spring; dust storms; sandstorms

ECU.terrain: coastal plain (costa), inter-Andean central highlands (sierra), and flat to rolling eastern jungle (oriente)
ECU.climate_text: tropical along coast, becoming cooler inland at higher elevations; tropical in Amazonian jungle lowlands
ECU.hazards_text: frequent earthquakes; landslides; volcanic activity; floods; periodic droughts. Volcanoes: volcanic activity concentrated along the Andes Mountains; Sangay (5,230 m) is mainland Ecuador's most active volcano; other historically active volcanoes in the Andes include Antisana, Cayambe, Chacana, Cotopaxi, Guagua Pichincha, Reventador, Sumaco, and Tungurahua; Fernandina (1,476 m), a shield volcano, is the most active of the many Galapagos volcanoes; other historically active Galapagos volcanoes include Wolf, Sierra Negra, Cerro Azul, Pinta, Marchena, and Santiago

DMA.climate_text: tropical; moderated by northeast trade winds; heavy rainfall
DMA.hazards_text: flash floods are a constant threat; destructive hurricanes can be expected during the late summer months. Volcanoes: Dominica lies in the middle of the volcanic-island arc of the Lesser Antilles that extends from the island of Saba in the north to Grenada in the south; of the 16 volcanoes that make up this arc, five are located on Dominica, more than any other island in the Caribbean: Morne aux Diables (861 m), Morne Diablotins (1,430 m), Morne Trois Pitons (1,387 m), Watt Mountain (1,224 m), which last erupted in 1997, and Morne Plat Pays (940 m); the two best-known volcanic features on Dominica, the Valley of Desolation and the Boiling Lake thermal areas, lie on the flanks of Watt Mountain, and both are popular tourist destinations

DJI.terrain: coastal plain and plateau separated by central mountains
DJI.hazards_text: earthquakes; droughts; occasional cyclonic disturbances from the Indian Ocean bring heavy rains and flash floods. Volcanoes: experiences limited volcanic activity; Ardoukoba (298 m) last erupted in 1978; Manda-Inakir, located along the Ethiopian border, is also historically active

FRO.terrain: rugged, rocky, some low peaks; cliffs along most of coast
FRO.climate_text: mild winters, cool summers; usually overcast; foggy, windy
FRO.hazards_text: strong winds and heavy rains can occur throughout the year

DNK.terrain: low and flat to gently rolling plains
DNK.climate_text: temperate; humid and overcast; mild, windy winters and cool summers
DNK.hazards_text: flooding is a threat in some areas of the country (e.g., parts of Jutland, along the southern coast of the island of Lolland) that are protected from the sea by a system of dikes

CZE.terrain: Bohemia in the west consists of rolling plains, hills, and plateaus surrounded by low mountains; Moravia in the east consists of very hilly country
CZE.climate_text: temperate; cool summers; cold, cloudy, humid winters

CYP.terrain: central plain with mountains to north and south; scattered but significant plains along southern coast
CYP.climate_text: temperate; Mediterranean with hot, dry summers and cool winters

CUB.terrain: mostly flat to rolling plains, with rugged hills and mountains in the southeast
CUB.climate_text: tropical; moderated by trade winds; dry season (November to April); rainy season (May to October)
CUB.hazards_text: the east coast is subject to hurricanes from August to November (in general, the country averages about one hurricane every other year); droughts are common

HRV.terrain: geographically diverse; flat plains along Hungarian border, low mountains and highlands near Adriatic coastline and islands
HRV.climate_text: Mediterranean and continental; continental climate predominant with hot summers and cold winters; mild winters, dry summers along coast

CIV.terrain: mostly flat to undulating plains; mountains in northwest
CIV.climate_text: tropical along coast, semiarid in far north; three seasons - warm and dry (November to March), hot and dry (March to May), hot and wet (June to October)
CIV.hazards_text: coast has heavy surf and no natural harbors; during the rainy season torrential flooding is possible

CRI.terrain: sand and coral reefs and islands (cays)

COD.terrain: vast central basin is a low-lying plateau; mountains in east
COD.climate_text: tropical; hot and humid in equatorial river basin; cooler and drier in southern highlands; cooler and wetter in eastern highlands; north of Equator - wet season (April to October), dry season (December to February); south of Equator - wet season (November to March), dry season (April to October)
COD.hazards_text: periodic droughts in south; Congo River floods (seasonal); active volcanoes in the east along the Great Rift Valley. Volcanoes: the active volcano Nyiragongo (3,470 m) poses a major threat to the city of Goma, home to a quarter of a million people; it produces unusually fast-moving lava, known to travel up to 100 km/hr; Nyiragongo has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; its neighbor Nyamuragira is Africa's most active volcano; Visoke is the only other historically active volcano

COG.terrain: coastal plain, southern basin, central plateau, northern basin
COG.climate_text: tropical; rainy season (March to June); dry season (June to October); persistent high temperatures and humidity; particularly enervating climate astride the Equator

COM.terrain: volcanic islands, interiors vary from steep mountains to low hills
COM.climate_text: tropical marine; rainy season (November to May)
COM.hazards_text: cyclones possible during rainy season (December to April); volcanic activity on Grand Comore. Volcanoes: Karthala (2,361 m) on Grand Comore Island last erupted in 2007; a 2005 eruption forced thousands of people to be evacuated and produced a large ash cloud

COL.quake_max_place: near San Antonio del Estrecho, Peru
COL.terrain: flat coastal lowlands, central highlands, high Andes Mountains, eastern lowland plains (Llanos)
COL.climate_text: tropical along coast and eastern plains; cooler in highlands
COL.hazards_text: highlands subject to volcanic eruptions; occasional earthquakes; periodic droughts. Volcanoes: Galeras (4,276 m) is one of Colombia's most active volcanoes; it has been deemed a Decade Volcano by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior, worthy of study due to its explosive history and close proximity to human populations; Nevado del Ruiz (5,321 m), 129 km (80 mi) west of Bogota, erupted in 1985, producing lahars (mudflows) that killed 23,000 people; the volcano last erupted in 1991; after 500 years of dormancy, Nevado del Huila reawakened in 2007 and has experienced frequent eruptions since then; other historically active volcanoes include Cumbal, Dona Juana, Nevado del Tolima, and Purace

MAC.climate_text: subtropical; marine with cool winters, warm summers

HKG.terrain: hilly to mountainous with steep slopes; lowlands in north
HKG.climate_text: subtropical monsoon; cool and humid in winter, hot and rainy from spring through summer, warm and sunny in fall

TCD.terrain: broad, arid plains in center, desert in north, mountains in northwest, lowlands in south
TCD.climate_text: tropical in south, desert in north
TCD.hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan winds occur in north; periodic droughts; locust plagues

CAF.terrain: vast, flat to rolling plateau; scattered hills in northeast and southwest
CAF.climate_text: tropical; hot, dry winters; mild to hot, wet summers
CAF.hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan winds affect northern areas; floods are common

CPV.climate_text: temperate; warm, dry summer; precipitation meager and erratic
CPV.hazards_text: prolonged droughts; seasonal harmattan wind produces obscuring dust; volcanically and seismically active. Volcanoes: Fogo (2,829 m), which last erupted in 1995, is Cabo Verde's only active volcano
