CMR.terrain: diverse, with coastal plain in southwest, dissected plateau in center, mountains in west, plains in north
CMR.climate_text: varies with terrain, from tropical along coast to semiarid and hot in north
CMR.hazards_text: volcanic activity with periodic releases of poisonous gases from Lake Nyos and Lake Monoun volcanoes. Volcanoes: Mt. Cameroon (4,095 m), which last erupted in 2000, is the most frequently active volcano in West Africa; lakes in the Oku volcanic field sometimes release fatal levels of gas, which killed about 1,700 people in 1986

KHM.terrain: mostly low, flat plains; mountains in southwest and north
KHM.climate_text: tropical; rainy, monsoon season (May to November); dry season (December to April); little seasonal temperature variation
KHM.hazards_text: monsoonal rains (June to November); flooding; occasional droughts

MMR.terrain: central lowlands ringed by steep, rugged highlands
MMR.climate_text: tropical monsoon; cloudy, rainy, hot, humid summers (southwest monsoon, June to September); less cloudy, scant rainfall, mild temperatures, lower humidity during winter (northeast monsoon, December to April)
MMR.hazards_text: destructive earthquakes and cyclones; flooding and landslides common during rainy season (June to September); periodic droughts

BDI.terrain: hilly and mountainous, dropping to a plateau in east, some plains
BDI.climate_text: equatorial; high plateau with considerable altitude variation (772 m to 2,670 m above sea level); average annual temperature varies with altitude from 23 to 17 degrees Celsius but is generally moderate; average annual rainfall is about 150 cm with two wet seasons (February to May and September to November) and two dry seasons (June to August and December to January)

BFA.terrain: mostly flat to dissected, undulating plains; hills in the west and southeast; occupies an extensive plateau with savanna that is grassy in the north and gradually gives way to sparse forests in the south
BFA.climate_text: three climate zones including a hot tropical savanna with a short rainy season in the southern half, a tropical hot semi-arid steppe climate typical of the Sahel region in the northern half, and small area of hot desert in the very north of the country bordering the Sahara Desert

BGR.terrain: mostly mountains with lowlands in north and southeast
BGR.climate_text: temperate; cold, damp winters; hot, dry summers

BRN.terrain: flat coastal plain rises to mountains in east; hilly lowland in west
BRN.hazards_text: typhoons, earthquakes, and severe flooding are rare

BRA.terrain: mostly flat to rolling lowlands in north; some plains, hills, mountains, and narrow coastal belt
BRA.climate_text: mostly tropical, but temperate in south
BRA.hazards_text: recurring droughts in northeast; floods and occasional frost in south

BWA.lowest_point: junction of the Limpopo and Shashe Rivers
BWA.terrain: predominantly flat to gently rolling tableland; Kalahari Desert in southwest
BWA.climate_text: semiarid; warm winters and hot summers
BWA.hazards_text: periodic droughts; seasonal August winds blow from the west, carrying sand and dust across the country, which can obscure visibility

BIH.climate_text: hot summers and cold winters; areas of high elevation have short, cool summers and long, severe winters; mild, rainy winters along coast

BOL.terrain: rugged Andes Mountains with a highland plateau (Altiplano), hills, lowland plains of the Amazon Basin
BOL.climate_text: varies with altitude; humid and tropical to cold and semiarid
BOL.hazards_text: flooding in the northeast (March to April). Volcanoes: volcanic activity in Andes Mountains on the border with Chile; historically active volcanoes in this region are Irruputuncu (5,163 m), which last erupted in 1995, and the Olca-Paruma volcanic complex (5,762 m to 5,167 m)

BEN.terrain: mostly flat to undulating plain; some hills and low mountains
BEN.climate_text: tropical; hot, humid in south; semiarid in north
BEN.hazards_text: hot, dry, dusty harmattan wind may affect north from December to March

BLZ.terrain: flat, swampy coastal plain; low mountains in south
BLZ.climate_text: tropical; very hot and humid; rainy season (May to November); dry season (February to May)
BLZ.hazards_text: frequent, devastating hurricanes (June to November) and coastal flooding (especially in south)

BEL.terrain: flat coastal plains in northwest, central rolling hills, rugged mountains of Ardennes Forest in southeast
BEL.climate_text: temperate; mild winters, cool summers; rainy, humid, cloudy
BEL.hazards_text: flooding is a threat along rivers and in areas of reclaimed coastal land, protected from the sea by concrete dikes

BLR.climate_text: cold winters, cool and moist summers; transitional between continental and maritime

BRB.terrain: relatively flat; rises gently to central highland region

BGD.terrain: mostly flat alluvial plain; hilly in southeast
BGD.climate_text: tropical; mild winter (October to March); hot, humid summer (March to June); humid, warm rainy monsoon (June to October)
BGD.hazards_text: droughts; cyclones; much of the country routinely inundated during the summer monsoon season

BHR.terrain: mostly low desert plain rising gently to low central escarpment
BHR.climate_text: arid; mild, pleasant winters; very hot, humid summers

AZE.terrain: large, flat Kur-Araz Ovaligi (Kura-Araks Lowland, much of it below sea level) with Great Caucasus Mountains to the north, Qarabag Yaylasi (Karabakh Upland) to the west; Baku lies on Abseron Yasaqligi (Apsheron Peninsula) that juts into Caspian Sea

AUT.hazards_text: surrounded by shoals and reefs that can pose maritime hazards

AUS.terrain: mostly low plateau with deserts; fertile plain in southeast
AUS.climate_text: generally arid to semiarid; temperate in south and east; tropical in north
AUS.hazards_text: cyclones along the coast; severe droughts; forest fires. Volcanoes: volcanic activity on Heard and McDonald Islands

HMD.highest_point: Mawson Peak on Big Ben volcano
HMD.terrain: Heard Island - 80% ice-covered, bleak and mountainous, dominated by a large massif (Big Ben) and an active volcano (Mawson Peak); McDonald Islands - small and rocky
HMD.hazards_text: Mawson Peak, an active volcano, is on Heard Island

NFK.terrain: volcanic island with mostly rolling plains
NFK.climate_text: subtropical; mild, little seasonal temperature variation

ARM.terrain: Armenian Highland with mountains; little forest land; fast flowing rivers; good soil in Aras River valley
ARM.climate_text: highland continental, hot summers, cold winters

ATG.quake_max_place: near Saint John’s, Antigua and Barbuda
ATG.terrain: mostly low-lying limestone and coral islands, with some higher volcanic areas
ATG.climate_text: tropical maritime; little seasonal temperature variation
ATG.hazards_text: hurricanes and tropical storms (July to October); periodic droughts

AGO.terrain: narrow coastal plain rises abruptly to vast interior plateau
AGO.climate_text: semiarid in south and along coast to Luanda; north has cool, dry season (May to October) and hot, rainy season (November to April)
AGO.hazards_text: locally heavy rainfall causes periodic flooding on the plateau

AND.terrain: rugged mountains dissected by narrow valleys
AND.climate_text: temperate; snowy, cold winters and warm, dry summers

DZA.terrain: mostly high plateau and desert; Atlas Mountains in the far north and Hoggar Mountains in the south; narrow, discontinuous coastal plain
DZA.climate_text: arid to semiarid; mild, wet winters with hot, dry summers along coast; drier with cold winters and hot summers on high plateau; sirocco is a hot, dust/sand-laden wind especially common in summer
DZA.hazards_text: mountainous areas subject to severe earthquakes; mudslides and floods in rainy season; droughts

ALB.terrain: mostly mountains and hills; small plains along coast
ALB.climate_text: mild temperate; cool, cloudy, wet winters; hot, clear, dry summers; interior is cooler and wetter
ALB.hazards_text: destructive earthquakes; tsunamis occur along southwestern coast; floods; drought

SXM.climate_text: tropical marine climate, ameliorated by northeast trade winds, results in moderate temperatures; average rainfall of 150 cm/year; hurricane season stretches from July to November
SXM.hazards_text: subject to hurricanes from July to November

CXR.terrain: steep cliffs along coast rise abruptly to central plateau
CXR.climate_text: tropical with a wet season (December to April) and dry season; heat and humidity moderated by trade winds
CXR.hazards_text: the narrow fringing reef surrounding the island can be a maritime hazard

GIB.terrain: a narrow coastal lowland borders the Rock of Gibraltar
GIB.climate_text: Mediterranean with mild winters and warm summers
GIB.hazards_text: occasional droughts; no streams or large bodies of water on the peninsula (all potable water comes from desalination)

BVT.hazards_text: occasional volcanism, rock slides; harsh climate, surrounded by pack ice in winter

CCK.climate_text: tropical with high humidity, moderated by the southeast trade winds for about nine months of the year
CCK.hazards_text: cyclone season is October to April

TKL.terrain: low-lying coral atolls enclosing large lagoons
TKL.climate_text: tropical; moderated by trade winds (April to November)

TUV.climate_text: tropical; moderated by easterly trade winds (March to November); westerly gales and heavy rain (November to March)
TUV.hazards_text: severe tropical storms are usually rare, but in 1997 there were three cyclones; low levels of islands make them sensitive to changes in sea level

UMI.terrain: low and nearly flat sandy coral islands with narrow fringing reefs that have developed at the top of submerged volcanic mountains, which in most cases rise steeply from the ocean floor
UMI.climate_text: Baker, Howland, and Jarvis Islands: equatorial; scant rainfall, constant wind, burning sun Johnston Atoll and Kingman Reef: tropical, but generally dry; consistent northeast trade winds with little seasonal temperature variation Midway Islands: subtropical with cool, moist winters (December to February) and warm, dry summers (May to October); moderated by prevailing easterly winds; most of the 107 cm of annual rainfall occurs during the winter Palmyra Atoll: equatorial, hot; located within the low pressure area of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) where the northeast and southeast trade winds meet, it is extremely wet with between 400-500 cm of rainfall each year
UMI.hazards_text: Baker, Howland, and Jarvis Islands: the narrow fringing reef around the island poses a maritime hazard Kingman Reef: wet or awash most of the time; maximum elevation of less than 2 m makes the reef a maritime hazard
